_**User (2026-04-17 02:29:33Z)**_

Okay. This repository with its remote https://github.com/StefanoSanvitoGroup/MLdensity has last been updated in 2024. I am a collaborator that has been granted development access by the Sanvito group during my visit to them in summer of 2024. I was to develop the KKR-JLCDM extension, making the jlgridfingerprints compatible with my JuDFT.de group's JuKKR DFT code, for machine learning the JuKKR electron potential, rather than the VASP charge density, the original target. The development on both sides has stalled for a time, but now I am implementing the KKR side of things over at https://iffgit.fz-juelich.de/phd-project-wasmer/projects/vimp-prediction/ (preprocessing of JuKKR data to conform to what jlgridfingerprints expects). Now I am at the stage of actually using the jlgridfingerprints package in this repo here on my data. Hence I (go.fzj.de/wasmer, PhD candidate) recently started trying to install jlgridfingerprints again so that I can try it out. Together with Claude I noticed that the repository follows non-standard Python package conventions, both speaking in termas of general Python packaging and Cython extensions in particular. We came up with a way to update the packaging part of the code such that it conforms to conventional modern Python packaging standards. For this task I created this branch improve-packaging-setup. Once done and thoroughly tested on different architectures and properly documented, I want to create a pull request (PR) for it. What we have done so far is adding a bunch of new setup files that replace parts. However, there is still some work left to do. The end effect of this update will be that the package can be installed in one step (pip install .), rather than in several steps with implicit assumptions about file structures. The following is a summary of what was added so far and what is left to do, from previous Claude conversations which were not yet logged into this repo via specstory. **Files added at repo root (`MLdensity/`):**
- `pyproject.toml` — new file, declares build system (`setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__`), build dependencies (`setuptools`, `cython`, `numpy`), project name/version, and all runtime dependencies (replacing `jlgridfingerprints_environment.yml`)
- `setup.py` — new file at root level, replaces the one inside `jlgridfingerprints/`. Same Cython build logic but with paths adjusted to `jlgridfingerprints/src/*.pyx`, extension modules named `jlgridfingerprints.lib.*`, and proper `packages` and `package_dir` declarations (previously, Cython build had to be triggered manually via `cd jlgridfingerprints; LDSHARED="gcc -shared" CC=gcc python setup.py build_ext --inplace`)
- `Dockerfile` — for containerized use, default uv Python environment, alternatives (conda, venv envs) in `containers/`
- `.gitignore` - Updated w. standard Python repo entries, pre-existing entries  kept under category 'project-specific'

**Files changed in `jlgridfingerprints/`:**
- `lib/__init__.py` — needs to exist for Cython build & package import (create if not present, can be empty)
- `src/polynomials.pyx`, `src/jlcontraction.pyx`, `src/utils.pyx`, `src/geometry.pyx` — need to be checked for bare `from lib.* import` statements and patched to `from jlgridfingerprints.lib.* import` throughout (TODO)

**Files that become obsolete and can be removed:**
- `jlgridfingerprints/setup.py` — superseded by root-level `setup.py`, can be deleted
- `jlgridfingerprints_environment.yml` — superseded by `pyproject.toml` dependencies. This file was a conda lockfile or pinned environment file (created via conda env export by the original developer).

**Other files in need of update:**
- `README.md` - Update installation instructions. Assume uv Python env as default. Apart from just simple install & usage, also separately briefly describe the package layout, esp. the Cython part and build step. Separate subsection for containerized development. (TODO)

**Runtime steps after container start, assuming uv Python environment (no longer need separate Cython build):**
```bash
cd MLdensity
# user install
uv pip install .
# developer editable install
uv pip install -e .
```

```md
Paper **"Linear Jacobi-Legendre expansion of the charge density for machine learning-accelerated electronic structure calculations"** on [arXiv:2301.13550](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.13550)

Full data available (CHGCAR and POSCAR): https://zenodo.org/record/7599897#.Y_ZqoNJKiV4

## Installation

The recommended environment manager is [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

\```bash
# one-time install
uv pip install .

# editable install for development
uv pip install -e .
\```

This compiles the Cython extensions automatically as part of the build. No separate compilation step is needed.

### Alternative: conda / plain venv

\```bash
# conda
conda create -n jlchg python=3.11
conda activate jlchg
pip install .

# venv
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install .
\```

## Package layout

\```
jlgridfingerprints/
    __init__.py          # top-level package
    fingerprints.py      # JLGridFingerprints descriptor class
    predictor.py
    tools.py
    lib/
        __init__.py      # makes lib a sub-package
    src/
        polynomials.pyx  # Jacobi / Legendre polynomial evaluation
        jlcontraction.pyx# 2-body and 3-body contraction kernels
        utils.pyx        # vector norm, dot, versors
        geometry.pyx     # neighbour list (KDTree + PBC)
\```

The four `.pyx` files are compiled by Cython into shared libraries that land in `jlgridfingerprints/lib/` as `polynomials`, `jlcontraction`, `utils`, and `geometry`. The build is driven by the root-level `setup.py` / `pyproject.toml`; the old `jlgridfingerprints/setup.py` has been removed.

Build requirements (resolved automatically by pip): `setuptools`, `cython`, `numpy`.

Runtime requirements are listed in `pyproject.toml` under `[project] dependencies` and supersede the old `jlgridfingerprints_environment.yml`.

## Containerized development

A `Dockerfile` is provided at the repo root for a self-contained build. Alternative container definitions (conda, plain venv) are under `containers/`.

\```bash
docker build -t mldensity .
docker run --rm -it mldensity
# inside container:
cd MLdensity && uv pip install -e .
\```

## Usage

Play with the examples in the `aluminium/`, `benzene/`, `molybdenium/`, and `2d_mos2/` directories.

The second `RUN` keyword inside the shell command is the bug — `&&` chains shell commands, not Dockerfile instructions. Also, sourcing in `~/.bashrc` won't persist across `RUN` layers anyway; the right approach is to set `VIRTUAL_ENV` and update `PATH` via `ENV`.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-04-17 03:43:04Z)**_

This is a known rootless Podman issue — on macOS the volume UID mapping doesn't grant the container's root access to the host-owned directory. The fix is to add `:z` to the volume flag (relabels the mount for the container) or use `--userns=keep-id`.

1	Paper **"Linear Jacobi-Legendre expansion of the charge density for machine learning-accelerated electronic

6	## Installation
7	
8	The recommended environment manager is [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
9	
10	```bash
11	# one-time install
12	uv pip install .
13	
14	# editable install for development

17	
18	This compiles the Cython extensions automatically as part of the build. No separate compilation step is needed.
19	
20	## Package layout
21	
22	```
23	jlgridfingerprints/
24	    fingerprints.py       # JLGridFingerprints descriptor class
25	    predictor.py
26	    tools.py
27	    lib/
28	    src/
29	        polynomials.pyx   # Jacobi-Legendre polynomials evaluation
30	        jlcontraction.pyx # 2-body and 3-body contraction kernels
31	        utils.pyx         # vector norm, dot, versors
32	        geometry.pyx      # neighbour list (KDTree + PBC)
33	```
34	
35	The `.pyx` files are compiled by Cython into shared libraries in `jlgridfingerprints/lib/`. The build is driven by 
36	the root-level `setup.py` / `pyproject.toml`.
37	
38	## Containerized development
39	
40	A `Dockerfile` using uv Python environment is provided at the repo root for container managers (Podman, Docker). 
41	Alternatives for other Python env managers (conda, plain venv) are under `containers/`.
42	
43	```bash
44	podman build -t mldensity .
45	podman run --rm -v .:/MLdensity -it mldensity bash
46	# inside container:
47	cd /MLdensity && uv pip install -e .
48	```
49	
50	## Usage
51	
52	Play with the examples in the `aluminium/`, `benzene/`, `molybdenium/`, and `2d_mos2/` directories.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-04-17 03:56:14Z)**_

Yes, ignoring them is the right call here. The `.c` files are generated sources and the `.html` files are Cython annotation output (`annotate=True` in `setup.py`). Since `cython` is an explicit build dependency in `pyproject.toml`, there's no reason to ship the pre-generated C files — unlike projects that check them in specifically to allow building without Cython installed.
